claims.text: Solid TaVCrW has local chemical short-range order stabilized at approximately 800 K.
The SRO state is stabilized by approximately 2–3 meV/atom relative to a random solid solution.
An MTP can be trained on DFT data for the Ta–V–Cr–W system as a replacement for the EAM reference potential.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration in the proposed melting calculation.
MTP plus FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
MTP plus FEP will maintain a free-energy error below 0.5 meV/atom relative to TOR-TILD.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution by the MTP is the structural mediator enabling FEP.
The MTP must reproduce SRO configurations as part of the relevant phase-space distribution.
The MTP can provide near-DFT accuracy at a computational cost suitable for molecular dynamics.
The reduced cost of the MTP permits extensive sampling of both liquid and solid states.
FEP obtains free-energy differences directly from overlapping reference and DFT phase-space distributions, thereby bypassing the slow convergence of TI.
Training on diverse configurations allows the MTP to capture the approximately 2–3 meV/atom SRO stabilization energy.
The MTP training procedure captures electronic-excitation or density-of-states contributions that can shift the melting point by tens of kelvin.
A supercell containing at least 500 atoms is required to capture the relevant SRO correlations.
Calculations over 2000–2400 K are required to validate the SRO contribution.
The DFT calculations should use GGA-PBE with explicit treatment of electronic excitations near the Fermi level.
Including 0 K V and Cr configurations in the training set will avoid errors associated with GGA-PBE underbinding or overbinding.
GGA-PBE errors for V and Cr at 0 K may propagate into the predicted melting properties.
Neglected high-temperature magnetic fluctuations may cause additional shifts in the predicted melting behavior.
The hypothesis is falsified if the MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD solid–liquid free-energy differences for a MoNbTaW benchmark differ by more than 0.5 meV/atom at 2000–2400 K.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism state that electronic density-of-states or excitation effects are captured by MTP training, whereas the uncertainty field says electronic-excitation shifts may not be fully captured.
